operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case table/column names (Ref_Hotel_Star_Ratings, star_rating_code, hotel_id vs Location_ID) — must quote and compare case-insensitively.

Six subtype tables (Street_Markets, Shops, Museums, Royal_Family, Theme_Parks) have PK column that is ALSO an FK to Tourist_Attractions.Tourist_Attraction_ID — PK is a subset of parent keys, so child rows must be drawn from parent values, not fresh.
Tourist_Attraction_Features has composite PK (Tourist_Attraction_ID, Feature_ID) and both columns are FKs — composite-PK member max_l0=30 path applies.
Ref_Hotel_Star_Ratings.star_rating_code and Ref_Attraction_Types.Attraction_Type_Code are CHAR(15) but store digit strings '1'..'5'/'2','3','5','6','9' — String fuzzer, not Number.
Hotels.pets_allowed_yn CHAR(1) stores '1' and '' (empty string, not NULL) — String fuzzer with empty-string element.
Hotels.price_range REAL has mixed storage classes: real AND text ('' empty string present) — Number fuzzer will drop non-parsable, but original_values include ''.
Visits.Visit_Date DATETIME stores text 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' — dispatches to Date fuzzer (first element not int), template likely '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'.
Visits.Visit_Details VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL with distinct=1 and sample '' — single empty-string value, NOT NULL so empty string is legal.
Many VARCHAR(255) columns are 100% NULL (Other_Details, Description, Opening_Hours, other_hotel_details, Royal_Family_Details) — original_values all NULL, sampler drops None -> p:=1 fresh.
Small tables (2-20 rows) — original_values lists are tiny; rng.choices(k=min(5,len)) will repeat heavily.
Locations.Location_ID values are large (333..868) not 1..N — Number fuzzer range [-10^0,10^0] for INTEGER (scale 0) will produce tiny ints, far from originals.
All FKs have parent_exists=true; no dangling FKs, no self-references, no non-unique parents.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on INTEGER PKs: scale=0 -> range [-1,1] plus +-1/+-2 perturbation -> tiny ints (0,1,2,-1) vs originals 100-9000; implausible values drive FN on range/join predicates.

String fuzzer on CHAR(15) codes: fresh random strings over a-zA-Z0-9() length 0-15, plus contaminate — will not match '1'..'5' digit codes; joins to Ref_* still work via FK fill but WHERE star_rating_code='5' misses.

Date fuzzer on Visit_Date: template from first parsable element '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S', range 1980..2013 from originals; fresh dates uniform in that range — plausible, but p=0.2 element reuse means many fresh.
String fuzzer on names (Location_Name, Tourist_Details, Staff.Name): random charset strings, not realistic names — WHERE Name='Whitney' misses (FN).
Empty-string columns (pets_allowed_yn, Visit_Details): String sampler with element '' plus int-like +1/-1 additions; fresh draws rarely '' -> WHERE pets_allowed_yn='' may miss.
NULL-heavy columns (Other_Details etc.): original_values all None -> dropped -> p=1 -> always fresh random strings, never NULL; queries testing IS NULL will FP (TS never produces NULL there).
FK fill: child draws from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement -> duplicates in child FK columns; joins produce many-to-many fan-out, plausible for TS.

Subtype tables (Shops etc.): PK=FK drawn from Tourist_Attractions values -> PK uniqueness filter drops duplicates, so Shops rows are a random subset of attraction ids; queries joining Shops to Museums on id will find overlaps TS may or may not create.
Composite PK Tourist_Attraction_Features: max_l0=30 caps fresh draws, so (attraction,feature) pairs repeat -> PK dedup keeps first; coverage of pairs sparse.
price_range REAL: Number scale=4 -> range [-10^4,10^4] plus +-0.01/0.02; originals up to 7.6e8 — TS values far smaller; range predicates on price miss (FN).
Small tables (2-5 rows): choose_table_sizes gives 30-230 rows, far more than original 2-5; COUNT(*) queries will differ wildly (FP on count predicates).

checked/unique line-scan: UNIQUE (star_rating_code) line marks star_rating_code unique; drop_unique_duplicates will collapse Hotels.star_rating_code to 5 distinct values — matches original cardinality by luck.
